svg.title: Cognition Netlist — Verification and Invariants
svg.desc: Formal verification diagram. Preconditions, invariants, and observed results for each check in the repository, with the exact numbers from results.csv and capacity.csv, and the known gaps stated plainly. Green means the check passed as written; amber means the check is partial, unrecorded, or contradicted by the source.
svg.text: What is checked, what passed, and where the gaps are. Every number below is from the repository.
degree(v) = 8 for every vertex · edges = 4096 · components = 1 · energy non-increasing after forcing
max |z| < 5 · |z| relaxes toward 1 · overlap energy non-increasing per sweep (tolerance 1e-6)
Precondition: edges.txt is 8-regular, no self-loops, no duplicates, exactly 4,096 edges. Postcondition: all five verify.c scenarios PASS and the Hopfield benchmark completes 1,680 runs.
Energy scales as -0.05 per alive neuron. Noisy max|z| 1.0497 exceeds 1 during forcing, then relaxes.
Perfect recall holds to 32 patterns. At 64 patterns the memory breaks down sharply at high corruption.
Other checks that pass as written
Verilog testbench: syndrome 0 with no fault, non-zero with a 1-node fault. Two scenarios only.
Julia / R: PASS printed to stdout. Train RMSE on the same 600 rows. No split, no normalized RMSE.
Netlist: regenerated byte-identically by generate.c. SPICE transient run by the author in ngspice.
Graph: independently verified 8-regular, 0 vertices with degree not equal to 8.
Gaps and contradictions — stated, not hidden
(1u ^ 1u) is always 0, so it never checks GF(2) incidence parity.
Code trains on all 600 rows and reports raw train RMSE. No split, no normalization.
Manifest line 17 still says "NOT TESTED" for the ngspice transient; that line is stale.
Proof obligations — what is not proven here
The sampled spectral bound (5.26332 < 2 sqrt 7) is an empirical numerical check, not an exact Ramanujan proof. The graph is a seeded random regular graph, not a provably Ramanujan construction.
Liquid Haskell refinements in QuipperODELiquid.hs are declared annotations. No Liquid Haskell output or certificate is in the repository, so the no-cloning rejection is not demonstrated here.
The Quipper FSM nextState is partial: undefined (state, event) pairs have no clause and would fail at runtime. The Smalltalk FSM handles them by doing nothing.
The Verilog-A DAG syndrome implements LSB parity for unit coefficients only, while its header describes the general c1*c2 parity. The Verilog-A testbench has no automated pass verdict.
Nothing in this repository is a biological consciousness model, and no quantum effect is asserted. The work is a simulation artifact and a set of cross-language models.
